concurrency_findings.engine_support: Strata serves concurrent requests via --batch N slots with --batch-groups across a layer split; --batch-mtp (one MTP proposal per slot) is opt-in and requires ONE GPU, no layer split. /v1/status exposes concurrency.serving. Confirmed in src/program/generate.cpp and docs/BATCHING.md.

concurrency_findings.interpretation: On this launch/CPU-bound, expert-streaming workload, concurrency buys LATENCY-fairness (nobody waits for a whole answer) but NOT aggregate throughput. Two-GPU C4 aggregate (158 tok/s) barely exceeds C1 (150) and C2 dips below C1; single-GPU C4 aggregate (106) is flat-to-below C1 (111). Per-request decode falls ~4x at C4, likely because each verify window carries one token of every active slot (hypothesis consistent with docs/BATCHING.md; no profile or ablation isolating this cause was run). Two-GPU full residency (config A) gives the best solo throughput (~200 tok/s); the batch slots are for several concurrent agent requests, not for more total tokens/sec.
concurrency_findings.batch_slot_draft_note: Batch-slot requests report draft_n=0 in their .timings; the batch-slot timing path does not populate the per-request draft counters, so whether MTP drafts are active inside slots is UNCONFIRMED, not proven off. Solo (C1) path uses MTP drafts.
concurrency_findings.per_round_samples_note: One C4 config-B request stopped early at 97 completion tokens (finish_reason stop); its 102.0 tok/s is the solo-path promotion of the last remaining slot, not a batch-slot rate. Aggregate tok/s divides total completion tokens by total wall, so early stop is accounted for.

metric_definitions.aggregate_tok_s: sum of completion tokens over all requests in the round set divided by the total wall time of the round set (so it spans prompt time as well as decode; the driver labels it a decode rate because it sums tokens per second)
metric_definitions.per_request_decode_tok_s_median: median across requests of each request's own engine-reported .timings.predicted_per_second (decode only)
metric_definitions.distinction: the two are not interchangeable and are not compared to each other
metric_definitions.separate_experiment: the 227.4 tok/s full-VRAM clean MTP control cited elsewhere is a different run (two GPUs, no batch slots) and is not part of this concurrency comparison
metric_definitions.per_request_decode_falls_because: stated as a hypothesis; no profile or ablation isolated the cause

cpu_embedding_measured.verdict: CPU-only embedding of the small Qwen3-0.6B is REASONABLE for single/low-volume requests (20ms latency, lower than the GPU round-trip) but ~4.7x slower for bulk throughput. It is a valid tier for interactive/light embedding, not for large reindex sweeps. MXFP4 Jina acceleration is CUDA-only; it is not a CPU path.
cpu_embedding_measured.ratio_direction: GPU is 4.72x the CPU on bulk items/sec (183.1/38.8 = 4.72); equivalently CPU is 0.21x GPU (38.8/183.1 = 0.212). Single-request latency is the opposite direction: CPU 0.020 s is 4.05x faster than GPU-balancer 0.081 s (0.081/0.020 = 4.05).

embedding_findings.mxfp4_cpu_capability: cuda_embed_server.py raises RuntimeError if torch.cuda.is_available() is false and calls Triton matmul_ogs on cuda:0. The MXFP4 Jina build has no CPU execution path as shipped; 'CPU-only MXFP4 embedding' is not a supported mode. A CPU embedder exists but is the separate Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 model.
embedding_findings.strix_mxfp4: Strix has an RTX 5070 Laptop (8GB, CUDA) and an Intel Arrow Lake NPU (/dev/accel/accel0, render group). The MXFP4 Jina embedder needs CUDA, so it could run on the Strix RTX 5070 if VRAM and the Triton MXFP4 kernel support SM120 (Blackwell laptop); the NPU path is a separate, unverified question. Strix was probed read-only; no embedder was deployed there this turn.

service_incident_and_fix.trigger: After a benchmark restart, sindexer-embed-gpu@0/@1 crash-looped: kernels.get_kernel('kernels-community/gpt-oss-triton-kernels') raised 'could not verify publisher trust status'.
service_incident_and_fix.root_cause: The stored HF token at ~/.cache/huggingface/token (dated Oct 6) is INVALID. Anonymous GET /api/organizations/kernels-community/overview returns 200, but with the token it returns 401 Unauthorized; the kernels library sends the token, gets 401, and treats it as untrusted. This is fleet-wide (any host using that token), not caused by the benchmark. hf auth whoami reports 'Invalid user token'.
service_incident_and_fix.fix: Added a reversible systemd drop-in /etc/systemd/system/sindexer-embed-gpu@.service.d/hf-anon-trust.conf setting Environment=HF_HUB_DISABLE_IMPLICIT_TOKEN=1 so the trust check runs anonymously (200) and loads the cached Triton kernel. The credential file was NOT modified or deleted. Verified: kernel loads (KERNEL_OK True), both units active, :1236/:1237 serve the 1536-dim model, :1238 balancer round-trips a real embedding, sindexer update/search succeed end-to-end.
service_incident_and_fix.followup_not_done: The invalid token itself was not refreshed (needs the user's hf auth login --force with a valid token); the drop-in is a workaround that should be removed once a valid token is set.

The invalid HF token was worked around, not fixed; a valid token still needs the user's hf auth login.
No distilled candidate, model, or quality claim is made; this is serving-topology and embedding-tier evidence only.
